findings.title: Missing await on reserve_stock bypasses stock check
findings.explanation: reserve_fast is async but does ok = reserve_stock(...) without await. ok is then a coroutine object which is always truthy, so `if not ok` never raises 409, allowing oversell, unlike correct reserve() which awaits.

evidence.why: reserve_fast calls reserve_stock without await so ok is always truthy coroutine
reserve_stock is async def returning bool and must be awaited

findings.suggestion: Add await: ok = await reserve_stock(sku, quantity).
findings.verifier_note: Verified async def without await vs correct awaited call above; always-truthy coroutine bug confirmed.

findings.title: N+1 queries in /orders/details loops per-order fetch
findings.explanation: order_details does 1 query for all orders then 1 extra SELECT per order via db.items_for_order in a loop, so total queries are 1+N and grow linearly with order count.

evidence.why: Loop calls items_for_order once per order after list_orders
items_for_order executes one SELECT per order_id
list_orders is the initial 1 query before N queries

findings.suggestion: Fetch all items with a single JOIN/IN query for the listed order ids instead of per-order SELECT.
findings.verifier_note: Verified new endpoint does list_orders then per-order SELECT; N+1 confirmed and introduced by diff.

findings.title: Blocking requests.get in async endpoint blocks event loop
findings.explanation: remote_stock is async def but uses synchronous requests.get. This blocks the event loop while waiting for network I/O, stalling all other requests.

evidence.why: async endpoint uses blocking requests.get which blocks event loop

findings.suggestion: Use an async HTTP client (e.g., httpx.AsyncClient) or make the endpoint sync def.
findings.verifier_note: Verified async def with synchronous requests.get; blocking-event-loop claim true and new in diff.

findings.title: External HTTP call without timeout can hang endpoint
findings.explanation: remote_stock calls requests.get with no timeout. A slow or hung upstream blocks the worker indefinitely, causing DoS and resource exhaustion.

evidence.why: requests.get to external URL has no timeout argument

findings.suggestion: Add explicit timeout, e.g., requests.get(url, timeout=5).
findings.verifier_note: Verified requests.get has no timeout arg; distinct from blocking issue and directly actionable.
